candidates.title: Maersk raises Asia–Europe peak season surcharges
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will increase its Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) on shipments from Far East Asia to Northern Europe and the Mediterranean from a Price Calculation Date of 14 December 2026. For Northern Europe, the surcharge will rise to US$750 for all 20-foot containers and US$1,500 for all 40-foot and 45-foot equipment. The current levels, effective from 1 December, are US$500 and US$1,000 respectively. On the Mediterranean trade, the PSS will increase to US$1,000 for 20-foot containers and US$2,000 for 40-foot and 45-foot equipment. These rates are currently set at US$750 and US$1,500 following the surcharge introduced on 23 November. Separate euro-denominated levels will apply to shipments destined for Syria. The origin scope covers Brunei, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Cambodia, Mongolia, South Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. candidates.title: Ukraine plans another 15% rail freight tariff increase from 2027
candidates.excerpt: Ukraine plans another 15% rail freight tariff increase from 2027 Ukraine wants to raise rail freight tariffs again. The transport ministry has published a draft order that would increase the coefficients applied to domestic freight tariffs by 15% from 1 January 2027. The draft order covers freight transport by rail within Ukraine as well as related services. The ministry justified the tariff increase with the financial situation of the national rail operator Ukrainian Railways (UZ). Its revenues from ordinary activities do not cover the current costs of rail transport, the ministry said. The higher tariffs should also keep the transport process running without interruption under martial law and safeguard UZ institutional capacity and financial stability. That way, the company should remain able to handle freight orders, the ministry added. The increase comes at a time of declining volumes. candidates.excerpt: Fraught Coradia Max rolling stock programme pushes Alstom deep into the red FRANCE: Alstom has made a €954m first-half loss after major delays to its Coradia Max programme for Germany. Now Europe’s largest train maker is preparing to sell businesses and raise fresh money to cut its debt by €2bn. Publishing its consolidated results for the first half of its 2026-27 financial year on November 17, Alstom reported the net loss for the six months to September 30 against a €220m profit a year earlier, after problems with its Coradia Max double-deck trains forced it to slash expected margins on several major German contracts. With approval of the first of the six fleets now pushed back to March 2028, delivery payments have slipped too. candidates.title: ABF market reaches “new equilibrium” after shocks
candidates.excerpt: ABF market reaches “new equilibrium” after shocks The asset-based finance (ABF) market is returning to stability after a period of disruption, with appetite for funding recovering, according to UK consultancy Broadstone. Broadstone’s report, A New Baseline, is based on interviews with senior market participants, including lenders, funders and investors. It found that, after a prolonged period of reassessment, the market has reached “a new equilibrium”, with participants showing renewed confidence and a desire to grow safely. The research identified four trends shaping the market: confidence is returning, due diligence is becoming more demanding, funding is available but selective, and automation presents both opportunities and challenges. candidates.title: Momenta Finance launches working capital facility for UK SMEs
candidates.excerpt: Momenta Finance launches working capital facility for UK SMEs UK business lender Momenta Finance has launched a working capital facility to help small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) bridge gaps in their cash flow. Called Working Capital Finance, the facility offers between £50,000 and £500,000 over terms of up to 12 months, with rates from 1.25 per cent a month plus an arrangement fee. Momenta said the facility is designed to help SMEs buy stock and cover day-to-day running costs. The launch comes as cash flow remains one of the biggest challenges facing UK SMEs, with late payments continuing to tie up cash and hold back growth. In May, the government introduced the Small Business Protections Bill to tackle the problem. candidates.title: Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive arrives in New York
candidates.excerpt: MADRID, N.Y. — A significant piece of Northern New York’s railroad history has returned home to an enthusiastic community after spending decades in the Steamtown National Historic Site collection. Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive No. 210 was placed on its new display track at the St. Lawrence Power & Equipment Museum in Madrid on Nov. 20. “I feel elated,” said Roger Austin, the museum’s secretary and a driving force behind the project. “To have it finally come to full fruition is just very satisfying.” Austin worked closely with Steamtown officials to coordinate the transfer of the locomotive, necessary asbestos abatement and wheel repair work, and the truck move from Scranton, Pa., to the Madrid museum. No. 210, an Alco 2-6-0 Mogul, was built in 1923 for the Norwood & St. Lawrence Railroad. No. 202 was built by the Budd Co. in 1950 for the railroad’s Blue Bird, which ran between St. Louis and Chicago. Prior to relocating to the Branson Scenic, the car had been a regular on Lake State Railway’s office car specials in Michigan. candidates.excerpt: In episode 6 of the TrainsPRO Podcast, Trains Magazine Editor Bill Stephens sits down with intermodal analyst Larry Gross, president and founder of Gross Transportation Consulting. They discuss intermodal’s record year, the growth targets in the proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger, and the threat autonomous trucks pose to rail. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
